hypothesis_origin.same_species_replication: Signy Island Adelie concentration replication supported under the frozen three-error-model null
hypothesis_origin.extension_role: prospectively frozen cross-species test in declining chinstrap penguins at Signy Island
hypothesis_origin.external_context_known_before_effect: Published Signy analyses report long-term chinstrap decline; the exact nine-colony stable-roster total slope, effective-patch trajectory and concentration null result have not been inspected.

ecological_question: Is loss of breeding-patch diversity during population decline detectable beyond Adelie penguins, such that a declining chinstrap population also becomes increasingly concentrated among persistent breeding colonies?
prediction: Across the frozen nine-colony chinstrap panel, stable-roster total abundance declines and the effective breeding-patch number declines more strongly than expected under time-invariant colony shares plus independent counting error.

source.dataset: Population size and breeding success of chinstrap penguins on Signy Island from 1978 to 2020
source.support_audit: signy-chinstrap-concentration-support-v1 GitHub Actions artifact from PR 148
source.support_audit_boundary: schema, colony labels, seasons and numeric parseability only; breeding-pair magnitudes were not recorded or summarized and no effect statistic was computed

primary_window.rationale: The 1996 onward period follows standardized CCAMLR-era monitoring; complete seasons were frozen from outcome-blind numeric-parseability support.

primary_roster.selection_rule: Literal colony label spans both the first and last thirds of 1996-2019 and has a numerically parseable pair count in at least 12 seasons.
primary_roster.support_fact: All nine frozen units are jointly complete in the same 22 primary seasons.

decline_eligibility_gate.quantity: OLS slope of summed breeding pairs across the nine frozen colonies against actual centered season values in the 22 frozen primary seasons
decline_eligibility_gate.failure_rule: If the stable-roster total does not decline, the cross-species decline prediction is inapplicable and concentration support is false.

metric.name: effective_breeding_patch_number
metric.observed_statistic: OLS slope of annual effective breeding-patch number against actual centered season values across the 22 frozen primary seasons

fixed_composition_null.latent_composition: time-invariant pooled shares estimated from cumulative breeding-pair counts over the frozen nine-colony by 22-season panel
fixed_composition_null.annual_total: observed frozen-roster annual total retained for each primary season
fixed_composition_null.comparison: one-sided probability that a fixed-composition/error-only replicate has an effective-patch slope <= the observed slope

primary_decision.support_rule: decline gate passes, observed effective-patch slope is negative, and one-sided p <= 0.05 under all three frozen error models
primary_decision.failure_rule: any failed condition makes cross-species replication unsupported; no alternate roster, season set, label pooling, error CV, metric or tail may rescue the result

interpretation_boundary: Support would show cross-species recurrence of non-proportional breeding-patch contraction during decline; it would not identify individual dispersal.
Do not call internal N_eff a genetic effective population size or genetic effective number of breeders.
Do not attribute the chinstrap pattern to sea ice, krill, snow, predation, social attraction or competition without a separate causal test.
The already-known published species-level decline is context; the frozen stable-roster concentration endpoint is the prospective test.
